question.problem:
Which of the following are affine transformations?

I. ${T}_{1}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7u-v+6 \\ -7\end{aligned}]$

II. ${T}_{2}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}8v-9u \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}]$

III. ${T}_{3}:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}u-5 \\ 8u\end{aligned}]$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

With this in mind, let's look at each transformation in turn.

- Transformation ${T}_{1}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{1}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7u-v+6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7u-v \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}7 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Transformation ${T}_{2}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{2}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8v-9u \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-9u+8v \\ 4u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}-9 & 8 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In fact, the transformation ${T}_{2}$ is a linear transformation.

- Transformation ${T}_{3}$ is affine. Notice that ${T}_{3}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}u-5 \\ 8u\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u \\ 8u\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 8 & 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "${T}_{1},$ ${T}_{2},$ and ${T}_{3}.$"
